title: Gutter Software: Tools for Quotes, Measurements and Crews
html:
Gutter software comes down to three jobs: measure the house, send the quote and book the crew. A measurement app such as Hover, an estimate app such as Joist and a scheduling app such as Jobber or ServiceM8 cover all three. Add a website that brings in quote requests. Published monthly plans in this guide run from $0 to $149, and Hover Pro is $999 a year.

Gutter software has to turn a roofline into a price quickly. A homeowner who calls three gutter companies usually books the one that sends a clear number first. That makes measurements and quote speed the first things to fix, ahead of anything fancy.

This guide sorts gutter tools by the question each one answers. How long is the run? What do you charge? Who is on the crew? Did you get paid? Each tool shows the price its own vendor lists and one real limit.

Which gutter software measures a house and prices the job?

Hover and Joist split this job in two. Hover produces measurements from phone photos, and Joist turns your numbers into a clean estimate. Gutters price by the linear foot, so accurate runs and corners matter.

  • Hover: creates measurements and 3D models of a property from a phone scan, including gutters, roofs, siding and windows. Starter has no subscription and the first 3 projects are free. Pro is $999 a year and Business is $2,999 a year. A simple exterior scan lists at $59 on Starter and $39 on Pro. Limit: credits expire 12 months after deposit, and Hover does not send your estimate for you.
  • Joist: sends estimates and invoices and takes online payments. Basics is $10 a month and Pro is $17 a month on monthly billing, and Elite is $32. Limit: Basics allows 5 documents a month, so a busy installer outgrows it fast.

Do the math before you buy a scan plan. The Pro discount on a simple exterior scan is $20 ($59 less $39). At $999 a year, Pro needs about 50 simple scans to cover its price on that discount alone.

A small installer who measures by tape and quotes 20 jobs a year should stay on pay-per-scan or measure in person. A company chasing dozens of quote requests a month gets more from a plan. Hover is a measuring tool for exteriors, so cleaning-only companies rarely need it.

Which gutter business software schedules crews and dispatches installs?

Jobber, ServiceM8 and Workiz all schedule crews and send quotes, but they price very differently. One lists a free plan, one lists plans by job count and one asks you to request pricing.

  • Jobber: Core is $49 a month with no commitment or $29 a month billed annually, for one user. Extra users cost $29 a month each. Limit: card payments cost 2.9% plus 30 cents, and add-ons such as Marketing Suite at $99 a month are extra.
  • ServiceM8: Free is $0 for 1 user and 30 jobs a month. Starter is $29 for 50 jobs, Growing is $79 for 150 jobs and Premium is $149 for 500 jobs. Paid plans list unlimited users. Limit: each plan caps jobs per month, and Premium Plus charges 20 cents for each extra job.
  • Workiz: lists Standard, Pro and Ultimate plans with unlimited jobs, estimates and invoices on all three. Limit: no plan price is shown, since each plan says request pricing, so ask the vendor.

Count jobs before you pick. A gutter crew that books 40 installs and cleanings a month fits a ServiceM8 Starter plan with room to spare. A crew that books 200 stops a month needs the Premium plan or a different product. Remember that a cleaning route and an install job count the same on a per-job plan.

What software keeps gutter job photos and the books straight?

Two small tools fill the gaps after the quote: a photo app for proof of work and an accounting package for the books.

  • CompanyCam: stores timestamped photos by project and builds reports. Core is $63 a month billed annually, Crew is $129 and Scale is $199, with extra users at $29 each. Limit: Core includes one user and caps at two.
  • QuickBooks Online: Simple Start is $19 a month for the first three months, then $38. Essentials is $42.50, then $85, and Plus is $70, then $140. Limit: users are capped at one, three and five by plan.

Before and after photos protect you in a dispute over a downspout or a fascia board. Take a photo of every corner and every splash block before you start. That habit costs nothing, and the app only stores what the crew captures.

Which tools bring in gutter leads before the software matters?

Software runs the job after the call. Leads come from search, maps and ads. Google states that creating a Business Profile is free, which makes it the cheapest lead tool a gutter company can own.

Limit: a profile needs photos, accurate service areas and review replies to stand out.

Paid search can fill a calendar quickly in storm season. For channel ideas, see the gutter advertising guide .

How should a gutter company set up quote templates in its software?

Build one template per job type before you enter a single customer. Gutter quotes repeat the same line items, so a good template turns a ten minute quote into a two minute one.

  • Install by run: one line for linear feet, with corners, end caps and hangers listed as separate items.
  • Downspouts: a line for count and length, plus extensions and splash blocks.
  • Guards: an optional line priced by the foot, so the homeowner can accept or decline it without a new quote.
  • Removal: a line for tearing off old gutters, since disposal takes crew time.
  • Cleaning and repair: a flat visit fee and a per-story or per-foot add-on, kept separate from install templates.

Send the quote by text on the day of the visit. Most estimate apps, including the ones above, let the homeowner approve online. Ask each vendor whether the approval timestamp and the signed total are stored on the job.

Then connect the quote to the schedule. A signed estimate should create a job without retyping the address. If your tools do not connect, pick one scheduling app and let it also send the quotes, since double entry is where jobs get lost.

How do you run recurring gutter cleaning in the same software?

Recurring cleaning needs a route, a visit price and a reminder. Install work needs a quote, a deposit and a crew day. Treat them as two job types inside one app.

Check how each vendor counts a repeat visit. Job caps matter most here. On a per-job plan such as ServiceM8, each cleaning stop counts toward the monthly total. A route of 120 stops uses most of the Growing plan before one install is booked.

Seasonal peaks also change the math. Storm and fall leaf season can double your calls in a few weeks. Pick a plan that handles your busiest month, not your average one. A cap that blocks new jobs at peak season costs more than the plan upgrade.

How do you choose gutter software for your company?

Choose gutter software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it price by the linear foot, handle downspouts and guards as line items, and send a quote by text on the same day?

Cost: add the plan, extra users, job caps and card fees, then compare the total with one average install ticket.

Setup effort: can the owner build quote templates and import customers in one weekend, or does it need training?

Company typeStarting stackAdd next
Owner and one crew, mostly quotesJoist Basics or Pro, QuickBooks Simple Start, free Business ProfileServiceM8 Free or Starter
Two to four crews, installs and cleaningServiceM8 Growing or Jobber Connect, QuickBooks EssentialsHover plan and CompanyCam
Many crews, many quote requests a weekWorkiz or Jobber with more users, Hover ProMarketing support for lead flow

A one-crew shop should resist a bundle. Start with estimates and a free listing. Add scheduling when double booking costs you a job, and add measurement software when you quote more than you can measure by hand.

A multi-crew company should test dispatch on a live week before signing a year. Ask the vendor how a rescheduled job appears on the crew phone, and whether a customer gets a text with an arrival window.

A site with a quote form and a page for each service helps tools pay back. A website built for installers keeps quote requests flowing into the apps above.

What do gutter companies get wrong when they buy software?

The most common error is buying for the company you hope to be. A one-crew shop signs for a ten-user plan and pays for seats nobody uses. Buy for the next six months, and upgrade when a real limit blocks you.

The second error is skipping the card fee check. Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents, and on a large install that fee adds up. Ask every vendor for the rate, and ask whether bank payments are cheaper, since Jobber lists 1% for them.

The third error is treating software as a lead source, which it never is. None of these tools sends a homeowner to your door. Fix the quote process first, then spend on leads, so each new call meets a fast reply and a clear price.

What software does a gutter company need?

A gutter company needs a way to measure houses, send quotes, schedule crews and take payment. Start with an estimate app and a free Google Business Profile. Add scheduling once you book several jobs a week, and a measurement tool when quote volume outgrows tape and ladders.

How much does gutter software cost?

Published prices in this guide start at $0 for ServiceM8 Free and $10 a month for Joist Basics. Jobber Core is $29 to $49 a month, and Hover Pro is $999 a year. Card fees, extra users and job caps cost more, so confirm totals with each vendor.

Is Hover worth it for gutter installers?

It depends on volume. Hover Pro costs $999 a year and takes $20 off a simple exterior scan. It needs about 50 scans a year to cover that discount alone. Below that, Starter pay-per-scan pricing or an in-person measure is cheaper.

Can a gutter cleaning business use the same software?

Yes. Scheduling and invoicing tools such as Jobber and ServiceM8 work for recurring cleaning stops as well as installs. Watch job caps closely. ServiceM8 plans limit jobs per month, and each cleaning stop counts as a job, so count your recurring route before choosing a plan.

Does ServiceM8 have a free plan?

Yes. Its lists a Free plan at $0 for 1 user and 30 jobs a month, with text messages billed at 10 cents each. Paid plans start at $29 a month for 50 jobs, so a growing crew will pass the free limit quickly.

Do gutter companies need a website if they use scheduling software?

Yes. Scheduling software runs the work after a lead arrives, but it does not bring leads in. A website with pages for installs, cleaning and repairs, plus a quote form and a Google Business Profile, gives homeowners a reason to call you.

What should a new gutter company buy first?

Set up a free Google Business Profile and an estimate app first. Joist Basics at $10 a month or ServiceM8 Free are cheap starts. Add scheduling, photo and measurement tools only when missed bookings or slow quotes start costing you jobs.

What software does a gutter company need?
A gutter company needs a way to measure houses, send quotes, schedule crews and take payment. Start with an estimate app and a free Google Business Profile. Add scheduling once you book several jobs a week, and a measurement tool when quote volume outgrows tape and ladders.
###
How much does gutter software cost?
Published prices in this guide start at $0 for ServiceM8 Free and $10 a month for Joist Basics. Jobber Core is $29 to $49 a month, and Hover Pro is $999 a year. Card fees, extra users and job caps cost more, so confirm totals with each vendor.
###
Is Hover worth it for gutter installers?
It depends on volume. Hover Pro costs $999 a year and takes $20 off a simple exterior scan. It needs about 50 scans a year to cover that discount alone. Below that, Starter pay-per-scan pricing or an in-person measure is cheaper.
###
Can a gutter cleaning business use the same software?
Yes. Scheduling and invoicing tools such as Jobber and ServiceM8 work for recurring cleaning stops as well as installs. Watch job caps closely. ServiceM8 plans limit jobs per month, and each cleaning stop counts as a job, so count your recurring route before choosing a plan.
###
Does ServiceM8 have a free plan?
Yes. Its lists a Free plan at $0 for 1 user and 30 jobs a month, with text messages billed at 10 cents each. Paid plans start at $29 a month for 50 jobs, so a growing crew will pass the free limit quickly.
###
Do gutter companies need a website if they use scheduling software?
Yes. Scheduling software runs the work after a lead arrives, but it does not bring leads in. A website with pages for installs, cleaning and repairs, plus a quote form and a Google Business Profile, gives homeowners a reason to call you.
###
What should a new gutter company buy first?
Set up a free Google Business Profile and an estimate app first. Joist Basics at $10 a month or ServiceM8 Free are cheap starts. Add scheduling, photo and measurement tools only when missed bookings or slow quotes start costing you jobs.
